newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro steel works Feb output drops - Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro steel works Feb output drops - Tanjug.

text.p: Production of finished goods in Montenegro's iron and steel works Niksicka Zelezara dropped in February and prospects for it picking up in March are bleak, Yugoslav News agency Tanjug said Monday.

"Niksicka steel works produced 10,765 tonnes of finished steel products in January and only 4,459 in February... Chances for the situation improving in March are poor," Niksicka steel works director Vojin Djukanovic was quoted by Tanjug as saying.
He said there were over 8,000 tonnes of steel on stock for which the buyer was unable to pay so that about 35 million dinars ($6.17 million) worth of stocks were "frozen".

Uncontrolled imports of concrete steel, pipes, steel strips, plates and other products are still causing problems to the Niksicka complex, said Djukanovic, who is also president of the Montenegrin Chamber of Commerce.
In January, 12,813 tonnes of finished steel products worth around $9 million were imported, and another 4,000 tonnes in February, Djukanovic said.
He said the situation in ferrous metallurgy, especially in steel production, was deteriorating and that Yugoslavia's lack from international financial institutions aggravated the problem.

Djukanovic listed growing intra-company debts, shortage of foreign currency for imports of raw materials and semi manufactured goods, insolvency in public and other firms, the budget deficit and high taxes on wages as the main difficulties faced by the sector.
The Niksicka steel works earlier said it planned to produce 145,000 tonnes of finished goods in 1997 compared to 136,670 tonnes in 1996.
Crude steel output for 1997 was targetted at 125,000 tonnes, up from 121,000 tonnes last year.
